title: Revisit a topic only with an upgrade
statement: Bring early ideas and skills back later, but only with a real upgrade, because a return at the same depth adds practice but no new demand.
detail: The curriculum architecture BrainLift separates a strong spiral, where each revisit adds a real upgrade (a new representation, wider scope, greater abstraction, stronger warrant or more demanding transfer), from a weak one of annual re-coverage with tiny increments that wastes time rebuilding context (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback2/WF - Curriculum Architecture Br - 260713-123107.md`). The reading project's failure taxonomy lists a throughline that doesn't spiral as a failure class: claimed throughlines must recur at greater depth, not just be labelled (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`). An upgrade can be more depth, a new representation or domain, wider scope, more abstraction, harder transfer or a combination with earlier skills.
against: The same BrainLift keeps blocks rather than spirals where coherence and immersion are essential (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback2/WF - Curriculum Architecture Br - 260713-123107.md`, line 108). The same review's refutation defends the repeat as deliberate practice for automaticity: "**Adversarial refutation attempt:** This is by design — the FIND skill is practiced in two" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/SIM-REVIEW-D7-D8-D10-D12.md`, line 129); the finding was graded major, not failing. One case only: 'This is the only cross-lesson defect on record.' (shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md line 197), and it comes from the source's recollections rather than records (line 181).

Prerequisite order, spacing, compounding, repetition and difficulty progression all need at least two lessons in view.
A topic is taught once, at the right grade, by one owner. Re-teaching the same content at a higher grade forces the deeper pass to re-teach the basics.
Grade 4 deepens Grade 3's domains and hands off cleanly to Grade 5.

A linked earlier concept must appear in the later unit's retrieval, model, guided analysis, or synthesis; merely naming the old unit in metadata does not count. Revisit links are never graded before they are reactivated.
**F5: Fake cumulative review.** Detection: a revisit appears only as a label or recall question. Recovery: require the earlier mechanism to explain new evidence.
A revisit is not justified by shared vocabulary alone. It must make a prior mechanism useful in a new historical problem.
Overlapping boundaries are intentional; they let the next unit reinterpret transitions rather than create an artificial clean break.

The overlap among official periods is productive. Reconstruction can be studied as the culmination of Civil War change in Unit 5 and as a starting condition for the New South and industrial order in Unit 6. The course marks the purpose of a revisit so repetition compounds knowledge instead of merely presenting the same label twice.
